 If Sunderland 's Premier League game against Leeds on Sunday had continued late into the night the wise money would have been on the deadlock not being broken.
 Fast forward three days and with 11 changes, Sunderland's second string found the attacking spark that has been absent too often of late in what was a bonkers first half against Brentford in the Carabao Cup fourth round on Wednesday night.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Black Cats could so easily have been three goals down after 25 minutes but instead found themselves three up after 40. Callum Wilson cut the deficit just before the interval and Igor Thiago headed in a second for the Bees deep in second half stoppage time, but Sunderland saw it out and and are now just two rounds and three games away from Wembley.
 It's the first time in five years that Sunderland have reached the last eight of the League Cup and they've done so without their stars. The likes of Nordi Mukiele, Granit Xhaka, Noah Sadiki, Enzo Le Fee and Brian Brobbey all sat out on Wednesday night. In their absence, the fringe figures stepped up, nobody more so than Jocelin Ta Bi, who laid on all three of Sunderland's first half goals. Will he be in the starting line-up for the crunch game at Coventry on Saturday? Probably not. But he underlined his exciting potential here, as did Timur Tutierov, who again led the line and deserved his goal, Sunderland's second.
 It was Chemsdine Talbi – in the starting line-up for just the second time this season and the recipient of the loudest pre-match roar from the stands – who set Sunderland on their way, though he will never score an easier goal. Ta Bi's low strike looked destined to roll over the line but Talbi made sure from less than a yard out. Ta Bi's delivery from Malick Fofana's first Sunderland goal which made it 3-0 was exceptional.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The fact Le Bris made 11 changes and didn't include so many of his aforementioned stars in the squad at all told of this competition's standing in the Sunderland pecking order, but the Black Cats are now reaching the stage where they can dare to start thinking about silverware.
 This victory was also significant because it was just a second win in seven games and will crucially lift spirits ahead of the most important game of the season so far at Coventry on Saturday. Win there and Sunderland will be looking up after finishing October with a flourish. Lose and the success Sunderland are enjoying in the cup competitions will continue to be overshadowed by the fact they're propping up the Premier League table.
 Brentford made eight changes compared to Sunderland's 11 and on four occasions early on the visitors went close to opening the scoring, denied by poor finishing, misfortune and the brilliance of Melker Ellborg in the Sunderland goal. James Collins headed straight at the keeper from a free-kick before Malick Diouf picked our Igor Thiago, whose first-time finished flashed just wide of the right-hand post.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Black Cats had another lucky escape soon after when Jannik Schuster crashed a header off the crossbar and Michael Kayode hit the post on the rebound. A fierce Mamadou Sangare drive was then superbly kept out by Ellborg.
 The opener felt inevitable, and it duly arrived – but at the other end. Jules Ahoka led the charge on the counter and played the ball right into the path of Ta Bi. Hakon Valdimarsson got a hand on the winger's low drive but not enough to keep it out and Talbi made sure on the line.
 Brentford had a glorious chance to level immediately when the unmarked Wilson fired over from near the penalty spot, and Sunderland's second goal came just three minutes after the first. Ta Bi forced his way past Diouf on the right with the help of a slightly fortunate ricochet before displaying his awareness to pick out Tutierov for a tap-in. The cross for his third assist was superb, putting the ball on the head of Fofana at the back post to extend the lead to three.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The frustration for the Black Cats, having so quickly built such a commanding lead, was that it was cut before the interval, Wilson in the right place to benefit from Vitaly Janelt's miskick and finding the net despite the best efforts of Ellborg, who so nearly kept it out. Ellborg did extremely well to deny Brentford and Wilson a second just before half-time. The striker looked certain to tap in a cut-back from the left but Ellborg dived at his feet and did enough to keep it out.
 After the madness of the first period, the early stages of the second were low-key and short on opportunities. Not that Sunderland will have been bothered by that. Taking the sting out of the game suited the Black Cats. They had a big chance to secure their passage when Valdimarsson made a mess of an attempted clearance and played it straight to the feet of Chris Rigg, but the half-time substitute wanted too much time and too many touches and his shot was blocked.
 Brentford pushed for a way back into the game but Sunderland defended superbly. Luke O'Nien, off the bench for Omar Alderete, made a brilliant headed clearance on the goal-line. Thiago's header squirmed through the hands of Ellborg but Sunderland saw it out.
